newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Busy Hong Kong takes Deng's death in stride.
newsitem.headline: Busy Hong Kong takes Deng's death in stride.

text.p: Hong Kong people took the death of Deng Xiaoping in their stride on Thursday, with most saying the passing of the Chinese patriarch would have little effect on the territory.
"I think it won't make any big difference to the financial or political point of view," said office worker Mimi Chow.
"A power struggle may happen with the top leaders in China but I don't think it will have any effect in Hong Kong."

Some political analysts had predicted Deng's death would create uncertainty in Hong Kong, threatening stability during its delicate transition to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years as a British colony.

While the colonial government ordered all British flags to fly at half-mast in a gesture of respect and newspapers splashed "Deng Dead" across their front pages, the news seemed to cast few ripples across the territory's daily bustle.
"I think people are complacent," said shop manager Jean Ramsay. Few customers had been talking about Deng, she said, adding that she had often been the one to bring up the subject.
Shop assistant Pam Yau, who was born in Hong Kong but brought up in Britain, had no interest in Deng or his death.
Ko Chiu, 80, expressed grief at Deng's death.
"I couldn't sleep well the whole night. He was a great leader of our nation. He improved China," said Ko, who was among a group of elderly practitioners of tai chi, or Chinese shadow boxing.
But another resident, Auyeung Pak, 85, paused from his slow jog in a Hong Kong park to shrug off Deng's death.
"It's normal for a man of that old age. I'm not too sad." Many people said Deng had been politically lifeless for some time.

"To be cynical, he's probably been dead a long time -- they're just picking the right time," said banker Diane Lam. "They don't want to mess up with the takeover and it's bad to have it after the takeover."
Hong Kong's stocks rallied on Thursday, with brokers saying Deng's death had ended uncertainty that had plagued the market over the last few sessions.
The Hang Seng Index of blue-chip shares was up 1.96 percent to 13,363 points at midday.
